newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK people take to streets over islands dispute.
newsitem.headline: HK people take to streets over islands dispute.

text.p: About a hundred Hong Kong people took to the streets on Sunday to protest against the landing by a Japanese rightist group last week on disputed East China Sea islands that are claimed by China, Taiwan and Japan.

The row over ownership of the islands, known as Diaoyu in China and Senkaku in Japan, flared up after a group led by Japanese legislator Shingo Nishimura landed on one of the rocky islands on Tuesday and raised a Japanese flag.

Holding huge banners and shouting slogans, the Hong Kong protesters, led by the Action Committee for Protection of the Diaoyu Islands, accused the Japanese government of conniving with Nishimura and his group.

But the protest was non-violent, unlike last October when activists stormed into the Japanese consulate. Marching from Victoria Park to the Central business district on Sunday, the protesters later sent representatives to the office of Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, urging him to express their anger to Beijing.
The demonstrators also urged Beijing to send naval vessels to patrol the islands as a show of China's sovereignty.
